title: Thailand Cuts Visa-Free Stay to 30 Days: What Indian Travellers Must Know
excerpt: From September 15, Thailand replaces its 60-day visa exemption with a 30-day tourism-only category for 60 countries including India, with limits on land-border entries.
body:
• Thailand's 60-day visa exemption ends September 14. From September 15, 2026, travellers from 60 countries and territories — including India — get visa-free entry for tourism with a permitted stay of up to 30 days.
  • Land-border entries on the 30-day exemption are limited to two per calendar year (with exceptions for Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia and Singapore). A one-time 30-day extension remains available at local immigration offices.
  • The old scheme's provision for short-term business or urgent work entry has been dropped — the new exemptions are tourism-only — and Visa on Arrival has been narrowed to three nationalities: Azerbaijan, Belarus and Serbia.
  • The Indian Embassy in Thailand advises Indian travellers to carry a passport valid for at least six months along with confirmed return tickets, hotel bookings and an itinerary.

Planning a Thailand trip? The rules are about to change. From September 15, 2026, Thailand will halve the length of visa-free stays for tourists from 60 countries and territories — including India — cutting the permitted stay from 60 days to 30 days under a new entry framework published in the Royal Gazette on August 31.

What's changing on September 15

The Tourism Authority of Thailand (TAT) says new 30-day and 15-day visa exemption categories, plus updated Visa on Arrival eligibility, take effect September 15, replacing the 60-day measure.

Under the new framework, holders of passports from 60 countries and territories — a list that includes India, the US, the UK, China, Singapore, Australia, Japan and all 27 EU states — will be eligible for visa exemption for tourism with a permitted stay of up to 30 days. Nationals of Mauritius and Seychelles get a 15-day tourism exemption, while travellers from Peru, Brazil and South Korea will be granted 90-day visa-free stays, up from 60 previously.

Why Thailand is doing this

Officials say the move is part of a broader effort to curb crime involving foreign nationals. A string of recent arrests has included foreigners accused of drug offences, sex trafficking and operating businesses such as hotels and schools without proper permits. Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow said the plan to trim visa-free visits was part of a crackdown on individuals abusing the visa system by committing crimes in the country.

The reform follows a Cabinet resolution approved on May 19, 2026, and formal sign-off by Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul in his capacity as Minister of Interior on August 26. Officials describe it as a shift toward a single, clearly defined entry scheme for each traveller category. Tourism remains vital to the Thai economy — the country has drawn 20.9 million foreign tourists so far this year, though that is down 3% on the same period in 2025.

The fine print for Indian travellers

For Indian passport holders, the 30-day visa-free entry replaces the existing arrangement from September 15. The Indian Embassy in Thailand has issued an advisory asking travellers to carry a passport valid for at least six months, confirmed return tickets, hotel bookings and an itinerary.

Two details deserve attention. First, travellers using the 30-day exemption to enter through a land border checkpoint will generally be limited to two such entries per calendar year — a constraint that matters for overland travellers coming through Myanmar, Laos or Cambodia. Second, the previous scheme allowed eligible travellers to enter for short-term business or urgent work purposes; that provision has been dropped, and the replacement rules are limited to tourism.

"Many travelers who have relied on the 60-day exemption for years will need to reassess their plans well before mid-September. The distinction between tourism and short-term work or business entry is now much sharper under the new rules."

— Rex Baay, Senior Immigration Consultant, Siam Legal International

Background: a revolving visa door

Thailand's entry rules for Indians have whipsawed in recent years. Indian travellers went from visa-on-arrival to a 60-day visa exemption, then briefly lost it before it was restored — each swing followed by visible changes in arrivals. The Livemint report on the earlier U-turn noted a noticeable decline in Indian arrivals after the 60-day exemption was discontinued, underscoring how sensitive the India–Thailand corridor is to entry friction. The current 30-day settlement is Bangkok's attempt at a stable middle ground.

What's next

The changes bite just as the festive and winter travel season ramps up — peak months for Indian leisure travel to Thailand. Travellers with long-stay plans can still apply for a one-time 30-day extension at a Thai immigration office, subject to officer approval, but anyone planning back-to-back land-border trips or mixing business with a visa-exempt entry should confirm their status with Thai consular authorities before booking. Watch Thailand's arrival numbers in the coming months: they will be the first real test of whether a shorter welcome mat costs the kingdom tourists.
image_caption: A graphic confirms Thailand's new 30-day and 15-day visa exemption rules. From September 15, Indian tourists get visa-free entry for up to 30 days, down from 60.
nri_angle: Thailand is among the most popular short-haul leisure destinations for Indians; NRIs and resident Indians planning festive-season trips should confirm entry rules before booking.
